clue.text: Copying an older style of rap

blocks.note: repro is short for reproduction, a copy made in a period style
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician borrowing an old-school flavour of rap for their own track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rap' looks like the music genre being copied, but it is the definition, in its sense of a sharp telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A rap over the knuckles is a rebuke, and a reproof is exactly such a rebuke.

clue.text: Travellers on international flight

blocks.note: surface reading: passengers aboard a plane crossing borders
setter's reading: flight as fleeing, so people escaping their country

explanation.walkthrough: Flight suggests an airliner; here it means running away, so these travellers are fleeing across borders.
explanation.definitionFit: People who flee their homeland for safety abroad are making a flight in the escaping sense.

clue.text: Picture landing place on island covered with grass

indicators.note: something covered with a layer is wrapped inside it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: a port is where ships land
to grass and to rat both mean to inform on someone
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A painting of a harbour on an island with grassy banks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like vegetation but is the slang verb for informing to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrait is a picture, specifically one depicting a person.

clue.text: Gem shown by friend with ring on

blocks.note: a ring is round like the letter O
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A gemstone displayed by a friend wearing a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'on' puts the ring's letter above the friend.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is an iridescent precious stone, so it is a gem.

clue.text: See file with PM's fancy full title

indicators.note: fancy describes something elaborate and made up, so the letters are arranged into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to consult the paperwork bearing the Prime Minister's elaborate formal title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Full title' sounds like a name with honorifics; in law, title means ownership.
explanation.definitionFit: Fee simple is the legal term for absolute, unrestricted ownership of land, the fullest form of legal title.

clue.text: Sentimental drunken kiss on the mouth

blocks.note: a maw is a mouth or jaws
kiss as a drunk would slur it, with the hissing end smeared to sh

explanation.surface: A soppy drunk planting a sloppy kiss on someone's lips.
explanation.walkthrough: The kiss is said the way a tipsy person pronounces it, then placed after the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Mawkish means excessively or falsely sentimental, cloyingly emotional.

clue.text: Suit and tie

blocks.note: first meaning: to go well with, to correspond
second meaning: a sporting fixture, as in a cup tie

explanation.walkthrough: Suit and tie look like an outfit; they are two separate meanings, a verb and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the answer means to correspond or go with; as a noun it is a game or contest, which a cup tie is.

clue.text: Comedian crazy about girlfriend in Australian city

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps round another

blocks.note: a wag is a joker
gaga means mad
WAG, wives and girlfriends, is the British tabloid term for footballers' partners

explanation.surface: A comic infatuated with his girlfriend somewhere in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: WAG appears twice: once as a joker, once as the tabloid acronym for a sportsman's partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagga Wagga is a city in New South Wales, the largest inland city in that state.

clue.text: Prisoner misbehaving anytime having to scrub yard

indicators.note: letters that misbehave will not stay in their proper order
to scrub something is to cancel or erase it, so a letter is struck out

blocks.note: taken as written
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: A prisoner who acts up gets put on yard-scrubbing duty.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a punishment detail scrubbing the exercise yard; yard is only its abbreviation, removed from the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An inmate is someone confined in a prison or institution.

clue.text: Corporal punishment where it can't be seen

blocks.note: first meaning: a thrashing or beating
second meaning: concealed, out of sight

explanation.walkthrough: One word covers a beating and the state of being concealed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiding is a thrashing; to be in hiding is to be concealed where nobody can see.

clue.text: The sky beginning to fall meant Mir tumbled

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter
something tumbled is thrown about and disordered

blocks.note: first letter of fall
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Mir space station plunging back to Earth as the sky began to fall.
explanation.walkthrough: Mir was the Soviet and Russian space station brought down in 2001, a neat surface for a sky clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Firmament is a literary word for the heavens, the vault of the sky.

clue.text: Flip a cat over, dead

indicators.note: turned over means flipped end to end, so the order runs the other way

blocks.note: taken as written
mog is British slang for a cat
D is the abbreviation for dead

explanation.surface: Tossing a cat into the air and finding it dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flip' looks like an instruction to turn things over, but it is the definition, meaning to lose your temper.
explanation.definitionFit: To flip is informal for losing control or becoming furious, which is what going mad means.

clue.text: Shoot group in anger management

indicators.note: a group in something sits inside it, so the letters lie within the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the boundary between the two words

explanation.surface: A shooting incident involving members of an anger management class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' suggests firing a gun; it is the noun for a young plant growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A germ is a bud or sprout from which a plant develops, as is a shoot.

clue.text: Cow police officers catch with net thrown over

indicators.note: something thrown over is flipped, so its letters are read back to front

blocks.note: DI is a detective inspector; plural DIS
to catch what someone says is to hear it
taken as written before turning

explanation.surface: Police throwing a net over a stray cow to capture it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' is the verb meaning intimidate, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to subdue their spirit, which is close to dishearten, to make lose confidence.

clue.text: Waste year boxing in Britain, barely covering expenses

indicators.note: boxing in means enclosing, as a box holds its contents

blocks.note: scrap is waste material
taken as written
GB is the abbreviation for Great Britain
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A wasted year in British boxing for a fighter barely earning enough to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxing' suggests the sport; it is the instruction to enclose, with waste and year wrapped around the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraping by is an idiom for managing to live on just enough money.

clue.text: Christian converted by pope in Calais

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Christian won over to the faith by a visiting pope in Calais.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converted' fits the religious picture perfectly, which hides its job of reordering letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An Episcopalian belongs to a church governed by bishops, such as the Anglican communion, a Christian denomination.

clue.text: Flowers round your neck bound to be relaxing

blocks.note: a lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers worn around the neck
surely expresses that something is bound to happen

explanation.surface: Being garlanded with flowers is sure to make a person relax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flowers' are not a river here; the whole phrase is one garland.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisurely means unhurried and easygoing, so a relaxing pace is a leisurely one.

clue.text: Massive failure to cut carbon

indicators.note: a cut goes into something, so one word sits inside another

blocks.note: coal is largely carbon
a loss is a failure, as in a defeat

explanation.surface: A huge failure in efforts to cut carbon emissions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carbon' tempts you to write C; it is the fuel made of carbon that gets cut open.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossal means enormous, like a colossus, so it fits massive as an adjective of scale.

clue.text: Clare regularly detains new cute RE teacher

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, taking every other letter
something new is made afresh, so the following letters are reordered
to detain someone is to hold them inside

blocks.note: second and fourth letters of Clare
the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Clare keeps the attractive new RE teacher after school.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is religious education, a school subject; it joins cute as anagram fodder rather than defining anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A lecturer is someone who teaches, especially at a university.

clue.text: Pub fed band uncut sandwiches

indicators.note: a sandwich holds its filling between outer layers

blocks.note: uncut means whole, intact
fed means ate
a ring is a band

explanation.surface: A pub feeding the band with whole sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandwiches' reads as food in a pub; it is a verb, the uncut word enclosing the others.
explanation.definitionFit: A watering hole is a humorous name for a pub, where people go to drink.

clue.text: Remove curse associated with blind pilot

blocks.note: effing and blinding is swearing; eff is the curse paired with blind in that phrase
an ace is a top fighter pilot

explanation.surface: Swearing at a blind pilot to get them out of the cockpit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blind' is not about sight: effing and blinding is British slang for swearing, so the curse linked with it is eff.
explanation.definitionFit: To efface is to erase or rub out, which is to remove.

clue.text: Somewhat useful sterling area that's partly in the EU

definitions.text: area that's partly in the EU

indicators.note: somewhat means to some extent, so only part of the following words is used

blocks.note: the letters span the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: Sterling is a useful currency in a region straddling the EU border.
explanation.walkthrough: Of the nine historic counties of this province, six form Northern Ireland, outside the EU, and three lie in the Republic of Ireland, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulster is the northern province of Ireland, split across the Irish border, so only part of it is in the EU.

clue.text: Dispute reduction in disease

blocks.note: a fall is a decrease
taken as written
gout is a painful joint disease

explanation.surface: A disagreement over a drop in disease rates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link inside the wordplay but supplies letters itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A falling-out is a quarrel, a breakdown of friendly relations.

clue.text: Start to gather wet crop

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of gather
rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: A farmer beginning to harvest a soaked crop.
explanation.definitionFit: Grain is a cereal harvest such as wheat or barley, a crop grown for its seeds.

clue.text: You mustn't put on TV before five

indicators.note: five is the Roman numeral V, so we want the letter standing just ahead of that one

blocks.note: to don clothes is to put them on
the letter in TV that comes ahead of the V

explanation.surface: A warning against switching the television on before five o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: Five is not a time: it is V, so the clue asks for whatever comes before V in TV.
explanation.definitionFit: Don't is the contracted negative command, equivalent to telling someone they mustn't.

clue.text: 17's gone an unnatural colour

definitions.note: the answer is a past participle; read as having gone an unnatural colour

indicators.note: entry 17 is someone who speaks to an audience, so this is what that person says

blocks.note: gone is a euphemism for passed away

explanation.surface: A teacher's hair has gone a strange colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is the lecturer, a speaker, so the word for gone is spoken and spelt as its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair that has been dyed has been coloured artificially, an unnatural shade.

clue.text: Giant flaps helping pilot in sharp turns

indicators.note: to flap is to get agitated and flustered, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Large wing flaps help a pilot bank hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flaps' suggests wing surfaces in the aviation picture; it is a verb for panicking.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti-g suit counteracts g-forces on a pilot in tight manoeuvres, preventing blackout.

clue.text: Answer with two affirmatives, one back to officer?

definitions.text: Answer with two affirmatives, one back to officer

blocks.note: surface reading: a reply consisting of saying yes twice
setter's reading: the reply a sailor gives back to a naval officer, ending with the form of address

explanation.walkthrough: The clue describes the naval acknowledgement: two old words for yes, then the respectful title for the officer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the traditional naval reply confirming an order has been heard and will be obeyed.

clue.text: Resistance occupies each French city before long

indicators.note: to occupy a place is to sit within it

blocks.note: EA is the abbreviation for each
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
Lyon is a city in France

explanation.surface: The French Resistance occupying every city in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The Resistance suggests wartime France; it is only the physics symbol, slotted between the two other parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Early on means at an early stage, near the start, so soon in a sequence.

clue.text: US singer takes Yankee Doodle allegro, skipping odd bits

indicators.note: skipping the odd positions leaves only the second, fourth and so on

blocks.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO alphabet
even-placed letters of the two words run together

explanation.surface: An American performer singing Yankee Doodle at a brisk tempo.
explanation.walkthrough: The US spelling has one L; allegro is a musical marking for brisk.
explanation.definitionFit: A yodeler is a singer who yodels; the single-L spelling is American.
